_comment_hooks: COMMITTED ON PURPOSE, so the rule binds the PROJECT rather than one
machine. Personal overrides belong in .claude/settings.local.json, which
is gitignored and is not touched by this file.
WHY: 'a green signal is only evidence about what it measures' is a
standing rule here, and this is its enforcement half. The gate has always
measured the right thing; nothing ever made running it unskippable. Four
incidents are behind that gap, and THREE OF THE FOUR were a claim about a
gate rather than a gate -- which is why the hook reads .gate-result.json,
written by tools/gate.py from the numbers it just computed, and never the
commit message.
NO 'if' FILTER, DELIBERATELY. The schema offers if: 'Bash(git commit*)'
to avoid spawning the hook for non-matching commands, but a prefix rule
would miss the compound form this project actually uses
(`git add -A && git commit ...`) and would not cover the PowerShell tool.
A guard that is cheap and wrong is worse than one that costs 200ms. The
script itself decides, on the whole command line.
PYTHON RESOLUTION (Windows): plain `python` is used because it resolves
on the PATH this hook inherits -- verified by firing the hook and
watching it block, not by assuming. If that ever stops being true on a
machine, replace the command with the absolute interpreter path, e.g.
.venv/Scripts/python.exe .claude/hooks/verify_gate.py
and leave this note saying which machine needed it and why.

hooks.statusMessage: Checking the gate result before committing
